correctness.rationale: For a Haar difference on the product of three circles the shortest representatives are independent uniform coordinates. Their exact squared-coordinate cumulants are 1/3, 4/45, 16/945; additivity and Newton identities produce the inverse cubic. Standard real-cubic discriminant and elementary sign arguments establish the complete feasible region, including repeated roots. A circle/plane intersection proves generic two-moment nonuniqueness; Rouché cluster counting proves a uniform 1/3-Hölder inverse, and two explicit near-cubic period families prove optimality. Standalone exact rational checks and independent random pair shortest-distance sampling passed. The proof, not numerical data, handles the infinite family.

value.rationale: The theorem answers an exact finite-data inverse problem inside a natural geometric class situated within a broader inverse-distance-histogram problem. It gives a complete semialgebraic admissible-moment region, proves precisely that two moments generically cannot suffice, and establishes an optimal global 1/3-Hölder inverse modulus under period bounds. Together these are a meaningful reconstruction and ill-conditioning classification rather than just a routine forward integral.
